title: Separated-source cancellation for a finite-inertia target
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Stacks in groupoids, Deligne--Mumford stacks, representability by algebraic spaces, and 2-fibre products have the meanings in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For a stack $\mathcal A$, its inertia $I_{\mathcal A}(T)$ has objects $(a,\alpha)$ with $a\in\mathcal A(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(a)$, and arrows $v:(a,\alpha)\to(b,\beta)$ with $v\alpha=\beta v$. The projection forgets $\alpha$. Finite inertia means that every scheme base change of this projection is a scheme finite over its base [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of Deligne--Mumford stacks over $S$. Suppose that $\mathcal A$ is absolutely separated, meaning that $\Delta_{\mathcal A/\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}$ is proper, and that $\mathcal B$ has finite inertia. Then $f$ is separated: the relative diagonal $\Delta_f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ is proper. Properness of these representable diagonals is tested on scheme charts [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No separatedness hypothesis on $S$ or on $\mathcal B$ itself is imposed.

source.place: Tag 050M (lemma-compose-after-separated), part (3), applied to the composite to Spec Z; Tag 0CL0 (lemma-diagonal-diagonal), part (1), makes the absolute target diagonal separated from its separated (in particular finite) inertia. This is the final separatedness argument of stacks-more-morphisms.tex Tag 0DUE.

proof.text: For every scheme $T\to\mathcal B$, the inertia pullback $I_{\mathcal B}\times_{\mathcal B}T\to T$ is finite by hypothesis and therefore proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. It is separated by the definition of properness in [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the representable map $I_{\mathcal B}\to\mathcal B$ is separated. Apply [lem-sfb-stack-inertia-separated-diagonal] over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to conclude that $\Delta_{\mathcal B/\mathbf Z}$ is separated.

Put $P=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$ and $R=\mathcal A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathcal A$. By [lem-sfb-stack-fibre-product-separated-comparison], $j:P\to R$ is representable by algebraic spaces and separated. The composite $j\circ\Delta_f$ is the absolute diagonal $\Delta_{\mathcal A/\mathbf Z}$: on an object $a$, both send it to $(a,a)$ with identity comparison. This is proper by the hypothesis.

Fix any scheme $T\to P$ and compose it with $j$ to obtain $T\to R$. Set $E=\mathcal A\times_R T$ and $Q=P\times_R T$. The map $E\to T$ is proper, since it is the scheme test of the assumed proper absolute diagonal; $Q\to T$ is separated, by the scheme-test conclusion of [lem-sfb-stack-fibre-product-separated-comparison]. Both are algebraic spaces. The factorization of the preceding step gives $E\to Q\to T$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-proper-cancellation] with $X=E,Y=Q,Z=T$: its composite is proper and its second map separated, so $E\to Q$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 050M (3), algebraic spaces A and B in the proof; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 04NX (2)

proof.text: The original map $T\to P$ gives a section $s:T\to Q=P\times_R T$. Pull back the proper map $E\to Q$ along $s$; [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] makes $E\times_Q T\to T$ proper. Associativity of $2$-fibre products identifies $E\times_Q T$ with $\mathcal A\times_P T$: a point of the left is an object $a$ with a comparison in $R$ whose image in $P\times_R T$ is identified with the specified section, equivalently a comparison $\Delta_f(a)\simeq t$ in $P$. The projections to $T$ agree. Thus every scheme base change of $\Delta_f$ is proper, which is precisely separatedness of $f$. All products over $R$ used the absolute base, so no separatedness of $S$ or of $\mathcal B$ was used.
